system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Subject to review of the complete SPA and due-diligence materials, the Buyer should respond as follows:

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap—preferably **50% of price**, with 100% or separate higher caps for core warranties—and no cap for excluded categories. | **Reject 20% and counter at 50%.** The cap is too low relative to the identified customer, IP, privacy and liability risks. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related claims and a **tipping basket**; no thresholds for title, tax, indemnities, covenants or fraud. | **Counter at AUD 10,000 / AUD 100,000 tipping basket.** Seller’s formulation could strand numerous commercially meaningful losses. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**. | At least **24 months**, preferably 36 months if there is no W&I insurance, with claims preserved once properly notified. | **Require a minimum 24-month period.** Eighteen months may not cover two full reporting/audit cycles or reveal latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental regime: **100% purchase-price cap**, no thresholds and at least six years to claim. | **Reject the general-warranty treatment.** The Buyer must be able to recover the full price if the Seller lacked capacity or good title to the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express carve-out; Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express exclusion from every cap, threshold, time bar, knowledge limitation and exclusive-remedy clause for fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate/wilful misconduct. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out.** The Buyer should not rely on uncertain implied or public-policy limits to protect it from dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable consequences; no general public-record disclosure. | **Delete general disclosure and require warranty-by-warranty specific disclosure.** A document dump improperly transfers disclosure risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Claims barred by Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge bar, or at most actual conscious knowledge of a short list of named Buyer deal-team members, without imputed, constructive or adviser knowledge and without a duty to investigate. | **Delete clause 8.3 or confine it to named-person actual knowledge.** “Discoverable” information is an unacceptably broad constructive-knowledge standard. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that associated conditions are satisfied. | A genuine Completion condition requiring unconditional consent, or consent on terms acceptable to Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied and no adverse amendment, payment or waiver. | **Do not deem the condition satisfied by mere delivery.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, making effective continuation critical to value. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release/discharge may be provided after Completion. | Repayment through Completion funds flow and simultaneous delivery of executed releases, security discharges, PPSR releases and control releases as Completion deliverables. | **Reject any post-Completion release.** A debt-free/cash-free acquisition cannot leave the Company indebted or its assets secured after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Seller-funded payment or dollar-for-dollar purchase-price reduction for bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, expressly shown in funds flow. | **Require full quantification and deduction at Completion.** Completion-triggered payments are transaction costs and must not reduce post-Completion cash or burden the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Pre-Completion payment and evidence of unconditional IP transfer, plus a specific indemnity covering ownership defects, infringement claims, remediation costs and associated losses. | **Make clean IP transfer a Completion deliverable and broaden the indemnity.** Paying the fee alone does not establish that Paperbark owns the Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unresolved. | Completed forensic/legal investigation before Completion, preservation of evidence, required notifications and remediation, plus a specific indemnity and retention/escrow for all incident-related liabilities. | **Do not accept a general disclosure-only solution.** The incident involves about 1,240 records and currently has unquantified regulatory, contractual and reputational exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 total—are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Evidence of terms, timing, accrual, cancellation rights and necessity; Buyer consent to renewal; appropriate working-capital, debt-like or price treatment for pre-Completion commitments. | **Reserve price treatment pending diligence and prohibit renewal without consent.** The disclosure does not establish that these commitments are ordinary, avoidable or properly accrued. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, pre-Completion covenants, Completion obligations, debt/leakage and fraud. | **Reject the global “all Claims” formulation.** Different risks require different caps, thresholds, survival periods and remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register as evidence of title to 100% of the shares. | Original/current register and certificates, ASIC and PPSR searches, evidence of legal and beneficial ownership free of encumbrances, valid transfer documents and releases of any security interests. | **Make independent verification and clean-title deliverables mandatory.** The Company’s register alone does not prove beneficial ownership or absence of encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are said to be “settled” under the general 20% cap and 18-month regime. | Separate tax indemnity and warranties—typically up to 100% of price and surviving about seven years—and enhanced IP ownership warranties/indemnities with longer survival and higher or separate caps. | **Reopen both regimes.** Tax exposures emerge after assessment cycles, while ownership of core IP is fundamental to an analytics business and already affected by Ironquay uncertainty. |

**Immediate Buyer priorities:** Bluefen must be secured before Completion; Riverlark must be discharged simultaneously at Completion; the bonuses and on-costs must be Seller-funded; and the Ironquay and privacy matters require specific protection rather than reliance on the general warranty regime.
=== END ADVICE ===
